purpose: Bounded paid-worker episode under consumer-directed Medicaid care, showing compensation, training, satisfaction, unpaid carryover, and durability concerns without pooling worker and beneficiary outcomes.

events.geography: United States; Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey Medicaid demonstration
events.date_precision: study-period reference date; worker interviews and wage measures were collected around nine to ten months after beneficiary random assignment with state-specific timing
events.denominator: Directly hired workers under consumer direction compared with agency workers; state and adult/child outcome universes vary
events.method: ASPE/Mathematica follow-up survey comparing directly hired Cash and Counseling workers with agency workers on hours, wages, benefits, training, satisfaction, strain, and preparedness
events.missingness: Worker identifiers, beneficiary linkage, exact care plan, long-run retention, replacement worker, household income, later wage path, collective voice, and exit are not retained in this compact record
events.exposure: A Medicaid beneficiary used consumer direction and hired a worker directly, often a family member or friend, rather than relying only on an agency worker
events.alternatives_before_action: Agency employment, unpaid family care, another paid worker, backup care, or no-care routes were possible; individual feasible alternatives are not fully observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Direct hiring created paid care work and scheduling flexibility, but many directly hired workers continued substantial unpaid care and had less formal training or benefits than agency workers
events.choice_or_response: Workers accepted direct employment, provided paid and unpaid care, and reported on wages, conditions, supervision, training, and preparedness
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The beneficiary was the formal employer and controlled hiring/scheduling within program rules; fiscal agents and counselors supported payroll and administrative tasks
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Consumer-directed Medicaid support created an alternative worker/payment route with fiscal counseling and payroll assistance
events.remedy_receipt: Worker interviews observe reported wages and working conditions at follow-up; individual payment completeness and timeliness are not verified in this compact record
events.durability_followup: Workers reported high satisfaction but the study raises concerns about wellbeing and willingness to continue over a longer period
events.immediate_outcome: Directly hired workers were generally satisfied with working conditions, supervision, and compensation; more than 40% were very satisfied with wages/fringe benefits, while many continued unpaid care
events.protected_outcome: Some family or friend caregivers converted part of existing unpaid work into paid work with flexible scheduling and reported preparedness despite limited formal training
events.sacrificed_outcome: Workers could receive lower benefits, less formal training, unpaid carryover, emotional/physical strain, and uncertain backup care compared with agency employment
events.cost_risk_transfer: Consumer direction transfers hiring, supervision, payroll, and continuity risk toward the beneficiary-worker relationship and household
events.later_outcome: The follow-up measures short-run worker experience but not retention, replacement, wage progression, injury persistence, beneficiary continuity, trust, action, or exit
events.meaning_and_attribution: Worker satisfaction and reported strain are measured; broader fairness, dignity, institutional legitimacy, and collective voice are not
events.public_or_collective_response: No worker organizing or political response is measured
events.counterexample: Worker satisfaction with a flexible paid role can coexist with modest wages, limited benefits, unpaid care, and uncertainty about continuing
events.source_and_uncertainty: ASPE, Experiences of Workers Hired Under Cash and Counseling, 2005; worker and agency comparison universes are study-specific and direct-hire workers are often relatives/friends who previously provided unpaid care

arrows.to: direct hire and flexible worker-control route
arrows.evidence: The ASPE report describes beneficiaries directly hiring and paying workers, deciding who provides care, when it occurs, and how it is delivered
arrows.counterexample: Not every treatment beneficiary received an allowance, hired a worker, or could find a worker
arrows.remaining_gap: Take-up, worker availability, beneficiary-worker linkage, plan completion, and backup care

arrows.to: reported worker compensation and job satisfaction
arrows.evidence: The report finds directly hired workers generally satisfied with working conditions and compensation, with more than 40% very satisfied with wages and fringe benefits across the states
arrows.counterexample: Satisfaction can reflect payment for work previously done unpaid and may not indicate adequate wage, benefits, or household security
arrows.remaining_gap: Individual wage adequacy, payment regularity, household dependence, and later wage path

arrows.to: unpaid care carryover and training/strain trade-off
arrows.evidence: The report states most directly hired workers continued substantial unpaid care; many received less formal training while generally feeling prepared, and the study identifies wellbeing concerns
arrows.counterexample: Lower formal training did not appear to compromise consumer safety in the cited health-outcome comparisons
arrows.remaining_gap: Paid/unpaid hours, physical and emotional strain, training quality, supervision, and care quality

arrows.from: worker satisfaction and flexible direct-hire arrangement
arrows.to: durable worker retention and beneficiary care continuity
arrows.evidence: ASPE identifies concerns about worker wellbeing and willingness to continue over a longer period, and notes that difficulty finding or keeping a worker is a primary dropout reason
arrows.counterexample: High short-run satisfaction does not prove long-run retention or a reliable replacement if the worker leaves
arrows.remaining_gap: Same worker-beneficiary follow-up, retention, replacement, care interruption, later wages, trust, and exit

boundary: This ledger adds the paid-worker/provider side of the Cash and Counseling system. It is not a pooled beneficiary or caregiver result and does not establish long-run worker retention, adequate pay, completed care, or household recovery.
storage_boundary: Only published ASPE study-level worker findings are retained; no worker, beneficiary, payroll, or Medicaid microdata are stored.
